integrate.idea: Make the durable HALT RECORD the spine of execution: whenever the trio blocks on a gate, the supervisor writes {run_id, gate_id, rendered_question, answer_grammar, resume_token, face_hash, opened_at} to the store. Nothing about a waiting run lives only in a process's memory or a terminal buffer.
integrate.criterion: C3 (real execution + validated handback); C5 (honest status)
integrate.note: FM01. This is the object every other halt idea hangs off; build it before any pre-answering optimization.

integrate.idea: Invert the wave order: schedule a wave that proves ONE real end-to-end HALT -> steward asks -> John confirms -> run resumes cycle against real Crucible BEFORE any wave that assumes unattended completion. Treat HALT as the normal path, unattended completion as the special case.
integrate.note: FM01. Sequencing constraint on the Stage-2 decomposition, not a feature.

integrate.idea: A gate answer IS a micro-commission: route gate answers through the SAME propose->confirm path as commissions, so there is exactly one confirmation code path, one `who` recording, one idempotency mechanism, and one ledger event shape for every human decision in the system.
integrate.note: FM01+FM02+FM15 collapse into one mechanism. Oranges: two confirmation paths would drift apart and one would end up unauthenticated.

integrate.idea: Resume mechanics: prefer Crucible's own checkpoint/resume (the engine already halts and resumes at user gates) over holding a blocked process alive on a pipe. The supervisor records the answer, then relaunches with --resume; a live-stdin bridge is a fallback only if resume proves lossy.
integrate.note: FM01. Falsify in Stage-1 by driving a real Crucible HALT/resume from a non-tty parent — the dogfood run already exercises this.

integrate.idea: Distinguish three non-running states honestly: `awaiting_human` (a halt record is open), `lost` (lease expired), `failed` (terminal error). A run blocked on a gate must never render as `running`.
integrate.note: FM01+FM07. 'Running for days' is the exact lie the North Star forbids.

integrate.idea: Stage-1 deliverable: a written GATE INVENTORY table — every Crucible approval gate and every Foreman blocker halt, with gate id, the rendered question text, and the accepted answer grammar. Anything not in the table is an unknown halt and must surface as `awaiting_human` with the raw prompt text verbatim.
integrate.note: FM01. Cheap now, and it also bounds FM02 (you cannot auto-pass a gate you have enumerated and ledgered).

integrate.idea: Make auto-approval structurally impossible: the Anchor->trio adapter builds argv from a typed allowlist with no free-form passthrough string, and a test asserts the constructed argv can never contain --yes/--auto-approve/-y for any input.
integrate.note: FM02. Structural, not a code-review convention.

integrate.idea: Gate satisfaction requires a signed confirmation record carrying real principal + gate id + face hash. Add the negative test: a run with ZERO confirmation records cannot reach Stage-2 output.
integrate.note: FM02. The test is the deliverable — prose about 'we never auto-approve' is worthless.

integrate.idea: Record every gate PASSAGE as a first-class ledger event, so an auto-passed or skipped gate is visibly ABSENT from the chain rather than silently indistinguishable from an approved one.
integrate.note: FM02. Makes absence detectable — the only defence against a silent deletion of protection.

integrate.idea: Every handback field carries PROVENANCE: {value, provenance: observed|synthesized|absent, source_ref}. receipt-validate.mjs validates the envelope; a separate provenance rule decides refusal. Store the raw trio output as a content-addressed blob beside it so any field is re-derivable.
integrate.note: FM03. Without provenance, 'validated' only means 'six strings were present'.

integrate.idea: Forbid synthesis outright for uncertainty_flags and human_wait — those two are absent-or-observed, and absent is a REFUSAL. grasscatch_why and tool_depth_why may be synthesized only with an explicit `synthesized` tag that renders visibly in the ledger.
integrate.note: FM03. These are the two fields the whole receipt design exists for.

integrate.idea: Extract, do not invent: derive handback fields from artifacts Crucible/Foreman ALREADY emit (run journals, HALT records, budget reconciliation, convergence rounds). If the artifact does not contain the fact, the field is absent — the adapter never fills a gap.
integrate.note: FM03. Also the way to honour the 'no trio changes' non-goal — read what exists rather than asking the trio to emit more.

integrate.idea: Ledger-level DEGENERACY CANARY: if N consecutive handbacks carry identical values for a field, flag the adapter as degenerate on the Roadmap and in the Strip. A silently-useless signal is worse than a missing one.
integrate.note: FM03. Oranges: this is the only mechanism that catches decay six months out, when nobody is reading.

integrate.idea: Make the trio-change trade an explicit Stage-1 DECISION-LOG entry: adapter-side extraction (honours the non-goal, may yield more `absent`) vs teaching the trio to emit the fields natively (violates the non-goal, needs an amendment). Decide it now, in writing, with the chosen consequence stated.
integrate.note: FM03 names this explicitly as a Stage-1 obligation. Recommend extraction; amendment only if extraction cannot reach uncertainty_flags.

integrate.idea: Move the guarantee to the CHOKE POINT: no job enters the runner without a valid, unconsumed confirmation token bound to (project_id, step_id, commission_hash, principal). Every start path either mints a token via confirmCommission or is rejected by construction.
integrate.note: FM04. Enforcement in confirmCommission alone only binds traffic that chose to be bound.

integrate.idea: Stage-1 deliverable: an exhaustive, written START-PATH INVENTORY — grep the runner's entry symbol across job_runner.py, terminal_session.py, lanes.py, every Node caller, every HTTP route, and every existing UI run button — with a negative test per path asserting an unconfirmed start is refused.
integrate.note: FM04. This is discovery work that must happen before decomposition, not during it.

integrate.idea: CLOSE, don't merely document, any start path that cannot be routed through the token check — delete it, or hard-disable it behind the same gate. An inventoried-but-open bypass is an inventoried hole.
integrate.note: FM04.

integrate.idea: Single writer made PHYSICALLY true: the Python execution side gets no write credential to roadmap_events at all. It appends status changes to an outbox it owns; a single Node writer drains the outbox and emits ordered roadmap_events with a monotonic per-run sequence.
integrate.note: FM05. Enforced by permissions/credentials, not by convention or code review.

integrate.idea: Read-side EVENT-ORDER INVARIANT: any projection that encounters a non-monotonic sequence or an illegal transition (complete before running, running after lost) raises rather than silently rendering a plausible-but-wrong Roadmap.
integrate.note: FM05. 'Wrong in a way that is not obviously wrong' is the failure this kills.

integrate.idea: Satisfy the hardening law explicitly for roadmap_events: name the atomic write, name the lock/serialization mechanism, and ship a concurrency test with N racing writers asserting one writer, ordered sequence, zero lost events. The claim is the test, not the prose.
integrate.note: FM05. Criterion 7 is worded as a storage claim — answer it as one.

integrate.idea: Storage substrate decision: authoritative ledger is SQLite in WAL mode on a LOCAL, non-synced path, with real transactional guarantees, instead of hand-rolled file locking. Any synced/OneDrive location is an EXPORT, never the source of truth.
integrate.note: FM14. Also removes a whole class of Windows rename-over-existing sharing violations.

integrate.idea: Refuse to start on an unsupported path: at boot, detect a synced/replicated store location and HALT with a clear message rather than corrupting quietly. Path support is a precondition, not a warning.
integrate.note: FM14.

integrate.idea: REAL-SUBSTRATE GATE: the concurrency and crash tests must run against an actual synced Windows path as a required gate; the clean local-CI run is kept only as a fast pre-check. A green test on a substrate the product does not run on is a false receipt.
integrate.note: FM14. Same family of self-deception as the auth-off suite in C6.

integrate.idea: Persist the ACCUMULATED FRAMING, not the chat: a structured, append-only draft-Face document with a stable draft id, one immutable revision committed per turn. This is state, not transcript — it does not violate the zero-chat-turns criterion.
integrate.criterion: C1 (fresh start, zero chat turns persisted)
integrate.note: FM06. Call out the distinction explicitly in the plan so a later reviewer does not 'fix' it away.

integrate.idea: Reconnect resumes framing: loading the draft id re-renders 'here is what I have so far; keep going.' Test = kill the Anchor process mid-framing, restart, resume, assert the draft is byte-identical.
integrate.note: FM06.

integrate.idea: Zero-chat-persistence PROOF: after a full stand-up, an automated check scans the store for any persisted dialogue turn (table, file, blob) and fails if one exists. Criterion 1's hardest clause gets a test, not an assurance.
integrate.criterion: C1 (fresh start, zero chat turns persisted)
integrate.note: Oranges: the draft-Face (I24) is exactly the thing a careless implementation would implement as a transcript. Test the boundary.

integrate.idea: Compile determinism receipt: record the compile inputs (draft revision hash, model, prompt version) on every face_rewrite_receipt, so a re-compile that diverges is visibly a different compile rather than an unexplained different Face.
integrate.note: FM06's second half — the trust loss comes from unexplained divergence, not from divergence per se.

integrate.idea: Face is CONTENT-ADDRESSED and append-only: every compile writes a new immutable version with a hash; the 'current Face' is a pointer. Every commission records the exact Face hash it was confirmed against, and the artifact viewer can always resolve that hash.
integrate.note: FM17. Without this, the audit trail cannot reconstruct what John approved.

integrate.idea: Derive face_rewrite_receipt as a DIFF between two immutable Face versions rather than trusting a narrative the compiler wrote about itself.
integrate.note: FM17. Same principle as I12: derive from artifacts, don't let the actor narrate its own behaviour.

integrate.idea: Test that mutating a prior Face version is IMPOSSIBLE (write-protected at the store level), not merely logged.
integrate.note: FM17.

integrate.idea: LEASE-BASED LIVENESS: a run is `running` only while its lease is fresh (tens of seconds). The run process renews a heartbeat; a reaper — not the corpse — flips an expired run to `lost`, a state distinct from both `failed` and `complete`.
integrate.note: FM07. This is the single highest-leverage mechanism for criterion 5.

integrate.idea: The UI must NEVER render `running` from a stored status alone — it renders from lease freshness. Encode this as an acceptance criterion on the Roadmap wave, not as a code comment.
integrate.note: FM07.

integrate.idea: Test liveness by SIGKILL, not by graceful shutdown, and assert the Roadmap reaches `lost` within the expiry window. Add machine-reboot and OOM variants.
integrate.note: FM07+FM16. A graceful-shutdown test proves nothing about the failure that actually happens.

integrate.idea: A `lost` step is RE-COMMISSIONABLE: reaping must release the one-in-flight-per-step constraint, or the truthful state still leaves John stuck. Test the full loop: kill -> lost -> re-propose -> confirm -> run.
integrate.note: FM07. Half-fixing this leaves the ledger honest and the project blocked.

integrate.idea: DETACH run lifetime completely: confirm enqueues a durable job record and returns immediately; a supervisor process owns execution and survives Anchor restarts; all run state is reconstructed from the store on reattach. The UI is a viewer, never an owner.
integrate.note: FM16. Also the precondition for I01 (the supervisor is what writes halt records).

integrate.idea: Test the three real detachment cases explicitly — browser disconnect, Anchor restart mid-run, machine reboot — and assert each ends in a truthful state (still running and reattachable, or `lost`).
integrate.note: FM16.

integrate.idea: Bind identity AT THE TOKEN: issue per-principal tokens (`john` vs `service`) and record resolved principal, token id, and issuance time on every confirmation. A service principal may NOT confirm spend — reject outright.
integrate.note: FM08. `who: 'anchor'` makes the load-bearing artifact of the whole North Star evidentially worthless.

integrate.idea: Auth must be checked on the STREAM, not only the handshake: assert token checks on SSE/WebSocket frames, artifact fetch, and event/projection reads. No token in a query string (it leaks into logs).
integrate.note: FM08. Long-poll/streaming endpoints are the classic hole.

integrate.idea: Auth-ON is the DEFAULT test mode for this surface: any test that passes only with auth off fails the wave. Given this surface shipped broken twice in one week, make ANCHOR_TOKEN-set the baseline, and auth-off the special case.
integrate.note: Criterion 6 is a stated repeat failure — invert the default rather than adding an extra pass.

integrate.idea: Assert on OUTCOMES not plumbing: each of criteria 1-5 gets one end-to-end auth-ON acceptance scenario that asserts the observable result (a Face exists with a north star; a step shows `lost` after SIGKILL), not that a function was called.
integrate.note: Criterion 6 says this in its own words; make it the shape of the acceptance criteria in Stage 2.

integrate.idea: FALSIFY classifyArtifact IN STAGE-1: take a real converged Crucible doc-trio off disk today, run it through classifyArtifact/buildArtifactCard, and record the actual result in the plan. Do not carry it as an assumption into a build wave.
integrate.note: FM09. Cheapest, highest-value falsification available right now — Crucible's own dogfood doc-trio is on disk.

integrate.idea: If classification fails, prefer option (a): the adapter emits a DOC-TRIO MANIFEST that presents as one artifact the existing classifier already understands. This honours the 'no bespoke plan template' non-goal — the manifest is packaging, not a new template.
integrate.note: FM09. Option (b) — amending the non-goal — is the fallback, and requires John's explicit approval at the lock.

integrate.idea: Version relationship as a FIRST-CLASS ARTIFACT: a re-commission carries the prior plan as an explicit input plus the correction as a scoped instruction, and the handback must include a changed/unchanged accounting keyed to stable wave/section ids.
integrate.note: FM10. Without stable ids there is no delta, and without a delta John hand-edits markdown and the ledger stops being true.

integrate.idea: Render a new plan version AS A DELTA against its parent by default, with the full document one click away.
integrate.note: FM10.

integrate.idea: Surface the honest limit at correction time: if Crucible cannot honour 'change only this' without a trio change, tell John 'this will regenerate the whole plan' in the confirm prompt rather than presenting a full regeneration as a targeted edit.
integrate.note: FM10. Honesty about a limit beats a pretend feature; also keeps the non-goal intact.

integrate.idea: The BOUND STEP is the most prominent element of the confirm prompt: step id, exact name, position in the roadmap, current status — and the confirmation must echo the step id back.
integrate.criterion: C2 (propose/confirm, commission FOR a named step)
integrate.note: FM11. Silent mis-bind is the worst failure class here: the ledger stays honest while the spend is wrong.

integrate.idea: Below-threshold or near-tie step matching REFUSES to propose and asks a disambiguating question instead. Refusing to propose is always cheaper than a confirmed wrong commission.
integrate.note: FM11.

integrate.idea: Log the match CANDIDATES AND SCORES on the proposal itself, so a mis-bind is auditable after the fact rather than being indistinguishable from a correct bind.
integrate.note: FM11.

integrate.idea: COMMISSIONABILITY as a compile constraint with a check: a roadmap step must be nameable as a single trio run with a bounded depth. Steps that fail are split at compile time or marked non-commissionable so the steward will not propose them.
integrate.note: FM12. Without it the commission unit is meaningless and John's confirm reflex calibrates to the trivial case.

integrate.idea: Carry an estimated SIZE CLASS on each step and require re-confirmation when actual spend exceeds the class. The class is a promise the runner keeps, not a label.
integrate.note: FM12+FM13.

integrate.idea: Enforce a REAL BUDGET IN THE RUNNER: token / agent-count / wall-clock ceilings passed into the trio invocation and checked by the process that owns the run, not by the trio itself. On breach: HALT and surface a re-confirmation turn ('used X of Y; continue?'), never silent continuation.
integrate.note: FM13. Crucible's Shark-Tank convergence loop is unbounded by design — a label on a screen will not stop it.

integrate.idea: Present the cost at confirm time as an explicit CEILING with a stated worst case, not a point estimate, and reconcile confirmed-ceiling vs actual in the ledger on every run so drift is visible over time.
integrate.note: FM13+FM21. An estimate John learns is wrong destroys the value of the whole confirm surface.

integrate.idea: IDEMPOTENT CONFIRM by construction: the proposal mints a single-use confirmation id; confirm is a compare-and-swap that consumes it, so a duplicate call returns the FIRST call's result rather than starting anything.
integrate.note: FM15.

integrate.idea: At most ONE IN-FLIGHT RUN PER STEP enforced as a uniqueness constraint in the store, not an if-check in application code.
integrate.note: FM15. Pairs with I34 so a reaped run releases the constraint.

integrate.idea: Test double-confirm the three ways it really happens: concurrent duplicate confirms, a confirm replayed after reconnect, and a confirm whose response was lost.
integrate.note: FM15.

integrate.idea: Operationalize the compile/plan bright line as a LINT OVER COMPILED FACES, run in CI: a roadmap step may name WHAT and WHY (outcome, rationale, size class) but must contain no HOW — no wave decomposition, no acceptance criteria, no sequencing of implementation work.
integrate.criterion: C1 (fresh start) + explicit non-goal ('nothing that makes the steward do the planning itself')
integrate.note: FM18. A checkable rule on the OUTPUT is the only defence against erosion with no single violating commit.

integrate.idea: Route every proposed enrichment of the compile through an explicit DECISION-LOG entry that argues the line. If a change makes the compile smarter about the work, it must justify why it is still not planning.
integrate.note: FM18. Crucible's own D1-D18 discipline applied to the steward's compile.

integrate.idea: BIND THE CONVERSATION AT CREATION and make it immutable: a conversation carries a required project id from its first turn; a conversation with no project id can ONLY do project selection or new-project stand-up. Every write asserts the target project id matches and refuses on mismatch.
integrate.note: FM19. Prevents a stand-up description from polluting a live north star that prior commissions were confirmed against.

integrate.idea: Render the bound project PERSISTENTLY in the dialogue surface — always visible, never inferred from context. The cheapest half of FM19's fix is a UI invariant.
integrate.note: FM19.

integrate.idea: Amend the North Star (or the non-goal list) to state explicitly: 'talking = typed conversational dialogue in Anchor; speech-to-text / audio input is out of scope' — and confirm that reading with John at the lock.
integrate.note: FM20. Meta-level: it protects the North Star's own readability rather than a numbered criterion. Cheap now, expensive at acceptance.

integrate.idea: Treat the CONFIRM SURFACE as the primary deliverable of its own wave: one screen stating WHAT step, WHAT will run, WHAT it may cost as a hard ceiling, and WHAT will change on disk. Acceptance test = John can correctly answer those four questions from the prompt alone, tested with a real proposal before the wave is GREEN.
integrate.note: FM21. This is the failure where everything works and John still will not use it — reflexive assent means the guarantee is in the ledger and absent in reality.

integrate.idea: On RE-confirmation, include 'show me what changed since the last proposal' — a diff of the proposal itself, not just of the plan.
integrate.note: FM21+FM10.

integrate.idea: Give the event stream a MONOTONIC CURSOR: clients reconnect with their last-seen sequence, and the server either replays the gap or instructs a full refetch. A reconnected client must never render a stale state that looks live.
integrate.note: FM22.

integrate.idea: Periodic RECONCILIATION on the client/projection: compare rendered state against lease freshness so a stale view self-corrects rather than persisting until someone reloads.
integrate.note: FM22+FM07.

integrate.idea: Keep the projection fully DERIVABLE from the event log at any time, and prove it with a replay test: rebuild from events, assert byte-identical to the live projection.
integrate.note: FM05+FM22. Also makes the ledger's 'single source of truth' claim mechanically checkable.

integrate.idea: Prove criterion 5 with the PARK/RESTART/KILL TRIAD as one scripted scenario — park to STATUS_IDLE, restart, kill — asserting the Roadmap step status at each transition. Criterion 5 names all three; test them together, not separately.
integrate.note: The criterion's own wording is the test plan.

integrate.idea: REHEARSAL COMMISSION (no-spend dry run): a proposal can be executed against a trio stub that exercises the entire path — token, supervisor, halt record, handback validation, artifact card, ledger events — without spending. Wiring gets proven continuously at near-zero cost.
integrate.note: Oranges: the expensive real run should be the last thing that finds a plumbing bug, not the first. Must be visibly labelled as rehearsal in the ledger so it can never be mistaken for a real run.

integrate.idea: One CHAIN ID threading commission -> confirmation -> run -> halt records -> handback -> artifact -> ledger events, so any single confirmed spend can be reconstructed end-to-end from the ledger alone.
integrate.note: Makes 'the campaign ledger remains the single source of truth' operational rather than aspirational.

integrate.idea: An in-Anchor 'AWAITING YOU' queue: every open halt record and every pending proposal surfaces in one place, so John never has to know a run is waiting. This is the in-scope form of 'notify me' — it lives on the Roadmap, not on a phone.
integrate.note: FM01's user-facing half. Without it, the halt record exists and nobody looks at it.

integrate.idea: Wire the GRASSCATCHER into correction turns: a spoken correction that is out of scope for the bound step is grasscatched (and grasscatch_why recorded) rather than silently widening the commission.
integrate.note: Reuses machinery the steward already has; also the anti-drift mechanism at the dialogue layer.

integrate.idea: Pre-answering static gates as an OPTIMIZATION LAYERED ON TOP of the resume channel — permitted only for gates whose rendered text exactly matches the Stage-1 gate inventory hash, and never for the three Crucible approval gates.
integrate.note: FM01 allows this explicitly, FM02 bounds it. The hash match is what keeps it from becoming auto-approve by another name.

integrate.idea: Add a NEVER-AUTO-RETRY rule: a `lost` or failed run is never re-started without a fresh human confirmation, no matter how obviously transient the cause. Automatic recovery would spend without confirmation.
integrate.note: Oranges: 'just retry the lost run' is the most natural convenience feature to add later, and it directly violates the North Star.

grasscatcher.idea: Speech-to-text / voice input for the steward dialogue.
grasscatcher.note: Explicitly excluded by I60's proposed amendment. Park it; do not let 'BY TALKING' be read literally mid-build.

grasscatcher.idea: High Seat portfolio altitude — cross-project reporting, global pause, resource-conflict arbitration between concurrent runs.
grasscatcher.note: Named non-goal (deferred). Note the one adjacency: the lease/reaper design (I31) is what portfolio pause would later be built on, so do not foreclose it.

grasscatcher.idea: Steward persona, livery, voice, or personality layer.
Mobile / iPad surface for confirming commissions on the go.
grasscatcher.note: Named non-goal, even though 'confirm from anywhere' is genuinely attractive given FM01's waiting-gate problem.

grasscatcher.idea: Full multi-user accounts, roles, and RBAC.
grasscatcher.note: The in-scope subset is I37 (two named principals, john vs service) — that is all criterion 2's `who` requires. Full RBAC is bloat by the inclusion test.

grasscatcher.idea: A cross-project spend analytics dashboard (burn over time, cost per project, forecasting).
grasscatcher.note: Portfolio altitude. The in-scope subset is per-run ceiling-vs-actual reconciliation (I52).

grasscatcher.idea: Push notifications to phone/email when a gate is waiting.
grasscatcher.note: Real value, wrong altitude for this North Star. I69 (in-Anchor awaiting-you queue) is the in-scope form; revisit notifications once halt-wait latency is measured.

grasscatcher.idea: Modify Crucible/Foreman to natively emit the six receipt fields.
grasscatcher.note: Directly violates 'no changes to Crucible/Foreman/researchPrime themselves'. Only reachable via the explicit amendment path in I14 — recorded here honestly rather than smuggled in as an adapter detail.
